clue.text: Pub mainly warm — and good nuts

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a warm person is kind

explanation.surface: A drinker praises a cosy pub and some tasty nuts served there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like bar snacks but is the definition, meaning crazy; 'mainly' cuts the last letter from KIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal ways of calling someone mad or crazy.

clue.text: One incarcerated in stir for bird

indicators.note: incarcerated means locked up, so this letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: to stir is to budge or move
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prisoner doing time in jail, with stir and bird both slang for prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' and 'bird' both suggest prison time in British slang, but stir means budge and bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar is a small pet parrot, an example of the bird kind.

clue.text: Surrender after Royal Engineers retreat

indicators.note: after places the giving-up word following the regiment

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to cede is to surrender or give up

explanation.surface: Army engineers are ordered to fall back after giving up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army, abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw, a synonym of retreat.

clue.text: Voice modulations without student's complaints

indicators.note: without means the learner's letter is removed

parts.note: inflections are changes in pitch of the voice
L is a learner, i.e. a student, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A singing student grumbles about voice exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates that British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints can mean illnesses, and infections are illnesses caused by germs.

clue.text: After golf, sit about wrapping female's presents

indicators.note: after puts the rest following the golf letter

explanation.surface: After a round of golf, someone sits wrapping a woman's presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SIT into ITS, which wraps round F to give IFTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Presents and gifts are synonyms for things given.

clue.text: Sad unemployment benefit total reduced

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

indicators.note: reduced tells us to shorten the word for total by its last letter

parts.note: total means full or complete

explanation.surface: A claimant laments that their jobless payments have been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is everyday British slang for state unemployment money.
explanation.definitionFit: Doleful is a synonym for mournful or unhappy.

clue.text: Lecture I'd set up ahead of second programme of study

indicators.note: set up in a down answer means raised, so the letters are read upwards

parts.note: the clue's contraction gives the letters ID
a course is a programme of study

explanation.surface: A tutor prepares a lecture before starting a second academic course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses ID, giving DI, in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal spoken or written treatment of a subject, like a lecture.

clue.text: Reported tragic king's lecherous look

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: King Lear is the title hero of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A tragic king is said to have given someone a lecherous glance.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king; his name sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, suggestive sideways glance.

clue.text: Hare grabbing a rodent, scratching tail very well

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: to hare is to rush, i.e. to fly

indicators.note: scratching means removing, so the word for rodent loses its last letter

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A hare catches a rodent and scratches its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hare' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning rush, FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Famously can mean excellently, as in getting on famously with someone.

clue.text: Left with pain, grow weak

parts.note: anguish is severe pain

explanation.surface: Someone left in pain begins to grow weak.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to lose vigour, fading or wasting away.

clue.text: On reflection, met for a drink

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to have met something is to have faced it

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, someone met up with a friend for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as 'after thinking'; here it reverses FACED.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is decaffeinated coffee, a beverage.

clue.text: Rod Hull used to be popular for such a worker

definitions.text: Rod Hull used to be popular for such a worker

parts.words: Rod Hull used to be popular for such a worker
parts.note: Rod Hull was a popular TV entertainer, but read as rod and Hull it evokes angling gear and the Yorkshire port once busy with trawlers

explanation.surface: A remark about the entertainer Rod Hull's former popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Hull was a British TV entertainer known for his puppet Emu; split up, a rod is tackle and Hull is an English port famous for its fishing fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who catches fish for a living uses a rod and worked from ports like Hull.

clue.text: Hesitancy from Parisian bandaging cut? On the contrary

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping round, so one piece goes inside another
this flips the stated order so the cut wraps round the French word instead

parts.note: an incision is a surgical cut
de is the French word for of, so a Parisian would use it

explanation.surface: A French nurse hesitates over dressing a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the French word would wrap the cut; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles so the cut does the bandaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecision is inability to make up one's mind, the same as hesitancy.

clue.text: Singer from Blur's inside repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the inner letters are written twice
inside means the letters of the band name without its ends

parts.note: Blur is the band name, with the apostrophe s standing for is

explanation.surface: A singer emerges from within the Britpop band Blur.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur is a British band; Lulu is a Scottish pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is a Scottish pop vocalist famous since the 1960s, an example of a performer.

clue.text: Overdone ham

definitions.meaning: exaggerated or melodramatic, as a performance can be
used as an adjective, over-the-top in the manner of a hammy actor

explanation.surface: A cooking complaint that the ham is overcooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overdone ham' looks like a kitchen disaster; both words are definitions about acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe exaggerated, showy behaviour typical of overacting on stage.

clue.text: At sea, hell's warlike predators

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Warlike, hellish predators roam the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the ocean picture but signals rearranging HELLS WARLIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcas are apex hunters of the ocean, preying on seals and fish.

clue.text: Around university, lesson is awfully low quality

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: poor standard

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the university letter
awfully suggests badly done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university lesson is criticised as dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles LESSON IS, and 'Around' puts the result round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Lousiness is the state of being very bad, inferior or shoddy.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvre — it's eaten by vulgar son

definitions.note: a singular course, defining a plural word for its pieces of raw vegetable

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside, so this word goes into the others

parts.note: crude means vulgar
it, with the apostrophe s standing for is

explanation.walkthrough: Hors d'oeuvre is the course; the answer is the plural name for its raw vegetable strips, so the number differs.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudités are raw vegetable sticks served with dips as a starter before a meal.

clue.text: A horse initially tried to drink

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone first tried to make a horse drink.
explanation.walkthrough: It recalls the saying that you can lead a horse to water but cannot make it drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: I perhaps alarm nun more if drunk

explanation.surface: A worry that a nun getting drunk would alarm someone even more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the numeral for one.

clue.text: Saw Chile without leaders for a short time

indicators.note: leaders are first letters, so each word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A traveller visited Chile briefly without its leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first letters off SAW and CHILE leaves AW and HILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Awhile is an adverb meaning for a brief period.

clue.text: Influence politician supporting one bill

indicators.note: in a down answer supporting means sitting below, so this piece follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
a bill passed into law becomes an act

explanation.surface: A politician backs a bill to gain influence.
explanation.walkthrough: A bill is draft legislation; once passed it becomes an Act.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact means effect or influence on something.

clue.text: River craft east of delta

indicators.note: in an across answer east means to the right, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A boat moves east of a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River craft' looks like a boat; 'River' alone is the definition, the Dart in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dart is a river in Devon, south-west England.

clue.text: I know miss struggles crossing river — this could describe the situation

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the river letter sits inside the rearranged letters
struggles suggests thrashing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits a missed attempt to struggle across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I KNOW MISS gives SINKOWIMS letters, with R put inside; the definition refers back to the clue's own struggling swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a do-or-die predicament, like one crossing a river who must either drown or reach the far bank.

clue.text: Boats, smooth and glossy, capsized

indicators.note: capsized means overturned, so in a down answer the word is read upwards

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: Smart, glossy boats have overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Keel can mean a ship in poetic usage, by the part standing for the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Keels can stand for whole vessels in literary use, the bottom timber naming the ship.

clue.text: He painted melting dial

definitions.note: a description of the artist, standing for the name

indicators.note: melting suggests a soft, changing shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist depicted a melting clock face.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls The Persistence of Memory, famous for its melting clocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist artist.

clue.text: Nancy's private conversation?

parts.note: Nancy is a city in France, so a private talk there would carry its French name

explanation.surface: Gossip asks about a woman called Nancy having a quiet chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman's name but is the French city, so the answer is a French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means head-to-head, a two-person intimate talk.

clue.text: Tea houses fashionable here?

indicators.note: houses means contains, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a country where tea is grown and drunk, and its fine porcelain once very fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The country where tea originated, famous for its tea houses.

clue.text: Boris's ending politicians' lies

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of the name is taken

parts.note: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party, politicians

explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party, which Boris Johnson once led.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories can mean untruths or fibs, as when a child is told not to tell stories.

clue.text: Striking is back, restricting a large hospital department

back means the little word is read in reverse

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
